findings.text: blocking: `_backend_serves_pair` treats any backend whose entry lane matches as serving every model the lane declares, so against the live configuration `crew queue edit --backend codex-anchored --model astra` (or `luna`) is accepted and stores model_key 'astra', while that backend's entry pins `model: gpt-6.1-sol`/`model_key: sol`, which is what dispatch_plan.resolve_role_override launches; ledger.backend_serving_model refuses the same pair, so this regresses a previous refusal into an accepted route whose recorded model the run will not use — the wrong-arm harm the commit message cites. The final clause should require the backend be the lane's own entry, as the docstring states.

non-blocking: the new `if backend:` branch requires the name to be an exact flight backend entry, so `--backend codex --model sol` — where `codex` is a catalogue lane and a declared backend with an empty body — is now refused, although _model_narrowed_backend (reckon/crew_dispatch_commands.py:660) resolved it to the serving `codex-anchored`; no test covers a lane-name spelling.

non-blocking: `_backend_serves_pair` duplicates the serving predicate owned by ledger.backend_serving_model (reckon/ledger.py:340-379) instead of extending it, and the copy drops the owner's requirement that the fallback backend be the lane's own — the divergence that permits the blocking finding above.
